vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.tool: Applies a group of Minecraft and VulkanMod settings for the selected performance target.
vulkanmod.options.advCulling.tooltip: Use a culling algorithm that might improve performance by reducing the number of non visible chunk sections rendered.
vulkanmod.options.ao.subBlock.tooltip: ON (Sub-block): Enables smooth lighting for non full block (experimental).
vulkanmod.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Enables culling for entities on not visible sections.
vulkanmod.options.frameQueue.tooltip: Higher values might help stabilize frametime but will increase input lag.
vulkanmod.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Reduces CPU overhead but increases GPU overhead. Enabling it might help in CPU limited systems. Unavailable on Intel GPUs and devices without multi-draw-indirect support.
vulkanmod.options.lodGpuCulling.tooltip: Culls distant LOD terrain cells on the GPU using frustum and depth-based occlusion tests before vertex shading. Only applies when a LOD companion mod is active and Indirect Draw is enabled.
vulkanmod.options.occlusionCulling.toolt: Skips rendering terrain, entities and LOD that are fully hidden behind other geometry, using a small depth grid of the previous frame. Replaces the old culling toggles.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveChunkUploads.t: Adjusts chunk upload work from recent frame time to reduce stutter while moving or flying.
vulkanmod.options.chunkUploadsPerFrame.t: Base number of built chunks uploaded to the GPU each frame. Higher loads terrain faster and stutters more.
vulkanmod.options.chunkFadeIn.tooltip: Newly loaded chunks dither in smoothly over the distant terrain instead of appearing instantly.
vulkanmod.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.tool: Use a unique render layer for opaque terrain to improve performance.
vulkanmod.options.particleCulling.toolti: Cull redundant particles based on distance, player FOV, and maximum same-type count budgets.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityCulling.too: Cull block entities (chests, signs, spawners, etc.) that are outside the camera frustum or further than 96 blocks.
vulkanmod.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Cull adjacent interior faces of leaf blocks to significantly improve performance in forests.
vulkanmod.options.connectedTextures.tool: Applies OptiFine-style connected texture rules from the loaded resource packs. Turning it off rebuilds the terrain.
vulkanmod.options.customItemTextures.too: Applies OptiFine-style custom item texture rules from the loaded resource packs, for named items and armour trims.
vulkanmod.options.renderScale.tooltip: The resolution the world is rendered at, as a percentage of the window. Lower means more frames and a softer image.
vulkanmod.options.vsrPreset.tooltip:
Renders the world below the window resolution, then reconstructs it to full size. Quality renders at 77%%, Balanced at 67%%, Performance at 50%%, each with the sharpening that suits it. Custom lets you set the internal resolution and the sharpening yourself.

This only helps when the GPU is the bottleneck, which in practice means with shaders enabled. On vanilla rendering the GPU is barely loaded and lowering the internal resolution costs image quality for no frame rate at all.
vulkanmod.options.vsrBackend.tooltip:
How the internal resolution is reconstructed.

Bilinear is the plain reference filter: cheapest and softest.
FSR 1 reconstructs edges before sharpening: the crispest single frame, but high contrast edges can shimmer while the camera moves.
VTU accumulates several frames to rebuild detail: the most stable in motion, and it needs shaders to be enabled. Without them it falls back to FSR 1.
vulkanmod.options.vsrSharpness.tooltip: Contrast adaptive sharpening applied after reconstruction. It only affects edges, never flat areas, and never overshoots into halos. Set it to 0%% to disable it.
vulkanmod.options.shadersEnabled.tooltip: Enable Volcanic's native Vulkan post-processing effects.
vulkanmod.options.horizonFog.tooltip: Smoothly fades distant terrain into the sky right at the render distance edge to hide chunk borders. Lower values pull the fog closer to the edge and make it thinner; Off disables it entirely.
vulkanmod.options.disableHiDPI.tooltip: macOS: render at the display's logical resolution instead of the full Retina resolution. Much faster, slightly softer image. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.moltenVkAggressive.too: macOS: submits queues asynchronously, prefills Metal command buffers and allocates from a shared MTLHeap. Can raise frame rates and may hurt stability. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.externalLod.tooltip: Lets a LOD companion mod render far terrain through Volcanic. Safe bypasses the external renderer, Experimental draws its terrain through the Vulkan bridge. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.externalLodDraw.toolti: Draws the external LOD terrain. Turn it off to keep the bridge active while hiding its geometry. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.glLegacyBridge.tooltip: Keeps the legacy OpenGL draw path available for mods that still issue GL calls. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.glFboViewport.tooltip: Uses the framebuffer-object viewport convention for mods that render to their own render targets. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.title: Volcanic Graphics

vulkanmod.applybar.texture_reload: %d held, Apply reloads the textures, Esc discards
vulkanmod.applybar.swapchain: %d held, Apply recreates the swapchain, Esc discards

vulkanmod.details.empty: Select a setting to see what it does.
vulkanmod.ui.plugins.intro: Plugins are mods that add rendering features to Volcanic. Turn one off to rule it out.
vulkanmod.ui.plugins.empty.hint: A plugin is a mod that declares its settings to Volcanic. Installed ones show up here.
vulkanmod.ui.plugin.empty: This plugin has no settings to show.
vulkanmod.options.entityShadows.tooltip: Mobs and the player cast real shadows instead of a dark blob. Costs more than it looks: while this is on, the shadow map is redrawn every frame instead of being reused.
vulkanmod.options.windStrength.tooltip: Sways leaves and crops. At zero the shadow map stops redrawing every frame, which is worth real frames on its own.
vulkanmod.options.showFps.tooltip: Draws a small frame-rate counter in the corner. For the full performance panel with hardware and timing detail, use the debug overlay instead.
vulkanmod.options.showCoordinates.toolti: Draws your position and facing under the frame rate readout. Works without opening the debug screen.
vulkanmod.options.perfLog.tooltip: Writes a timing report to the log every two seconds: frame rate, frame and GPU times, the CPU-bound or GPU-bound verdict, and the upload, setup and terrain breakdown. This is what to attach to a bug report.
vulkanmod.options.vulkanValidation.toolt: Turns on the Vulkan validation layers, which report the exact API error when the GPU misbehaves. Costs frames and needs the Vulkan SDK installed. Requires restart.
vulkanmod.options.debugOverlay.tooltip: The vanilla F3 screen. Toggling it here is the same as pressing F3.
vulkanmod.options.vsrDebug.tooltip: Shows what the resolution scaler is doing, split across the screen.
vulkanmod.options.pbrDebugNormals.toolti: Paints surface normals directly, to check that a resource pack's normal maps are being read.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.scale: %s s of played frames, frozen while this menu is open · scale 0 to %s ms, taller is slower · a frame above the scale is capped and marked
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.fingerprint.not: what this capture was taken under
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.scene.note: the denominators behind the frame time
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.memory.note: unified on Apple Silicon, so RAM pressure is VRAM pressure
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.stutters.note: worst buckets in the window, and what happened in them
vulkanmod.ui.stats.note.terrain: Builder threads park once 128 uploads are pending, so meshing stalls until the renderer drains the queue. Stutter here is the queue, not your shader.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.note.memory: A buffer count that never falls is a leak, usually a plugin that forgot to free. Collections during the window line up with the strip under the graph.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.note.machine: These have tens of seconds of inertia. They explain sustained throttling, never a single stutter. For that, read the GC strip.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.findings.note: read from this window, not a checklist
vulkanmod.ui.stats.finding.gc: A collection ate the worst stutter
vulkanmod.ui.stats.group.time.note: the question a plugin author actually has
vulkanmod.ui.stats.advice: Read the split below before blaming your own code.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.stutter.caption: A bucket is flagged when its worst frame exceeds twice the median, or the median plus 5 ms.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.nosamples: No render-thread samples yet (%s in the buffer). Play for a few seconds and come back.
vulkanmod.ui.stats.profile: Inside the worst stutter — render thread, %s samples
vulkanmod.ui.stats.legend: Two minutes of played frames, frozen while this menu is open. Each column is 100 ms: the bar is the average, the lighter band its best and worst frame, and the strip underneath is time lost to garbage collection.
vulkanmod.options.builderThreads.tooltip: How many background threads mesh terrain. More threads load the world faster and can stutter less, at the cost of CPU shared with the game itself. Auto uses half your cores.
vulkanmod.ui.experimental.intro: Features that are still being proven live here. They may cost frames, look wrong, or change without notice.
vulkanmod.ui.developer.intro: Diagnostics for reporting a problem: what your machine is, what the renderer is doing, and how the frames actually land.
vulkanmod.ui.favorites.empty: No favorites yet — click the star beside a setting to keep it here.
vulkanmod.ui.mods.empty: No installed mod exposes visual settings, and none has a settings screen of its own.
vulkanmod.ui.mods.passthrough: Volcanic found no visual settings to show for this mod.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.exclusive_fullscre: Only available in exclusive fullscreen. Set Window Mode to Fullscreen to pick a resolution and a refresh rate.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.launch_flag: A launch flag or a marker file is pinning this setting. Remove it to change this here.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.core_shader_pack: A resource pack is supplying its own core shaders, and they replace the shader pack while it is loaded. Remove that pack to choose again.
vulkanmod.overview.suggest_wait: Play for a few seconds and we'll suggest one
vulkanmod.overview.profiles_intro: Pick how the game should look and run. Try one, play a little, and the card remembers what you got.
vulkanmod.overview.profiles_legend: FRAMES how smooth it runs  ·  LOOKS how good it looks
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.perf: Sees 8 chunks · no clouds or shadows · flat light
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.bala: Sees 12 chunks · soft light · fewer particles
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.qual: Sees 16 chunks · clouds and shadows on
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.ultr: Sees 32 chunks · everything on · sharpest textures
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.perf: Lowest settings that still look like Minecraft
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.bala: Vanilla-like image, tuned for steady frames
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.qual: Fuller draw distance and smoother lighting
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.ultr: Everything on, for machines with headroom
vulkanmod.overview.advice.sampling: Close the menu and play for about ten seconds.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.capped_roomy: You are at your frame cap with room to spare. A higher preset is likely to fit.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.capped: You are at your frame cap. Nothing here will make it faster.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.server_tick: The world simulation is the limit, not the renderer. Graphics settings will not help.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.meshing: Chunk building never catches up. Look at render distance and chunk uploads first.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.gpu: GPU-bound. Render scale and shader settings are your levers.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.render_cpu: Render-thread bound. Render scale will not help; culling and chunk uploads will.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.idle: The renderer is mostly waiting. Something outside it is setting the pace.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.uneven: Your average is fine but frames are uneven. Look at chunk uploads.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.headroom: You have headroom at this preset.
vulkanmod.overview.advice.balanced: Nothing stands out. This configuration looks balanced on your machine.
vulkanmod.overview.hint.shader_pack: Your shader pack is a large part of that.
vulkanmod.overview.hint.far_terrain: A far-terrain mod is adding work.
vulkanmod.options.weatherRendering.toolt: Draws falling rain and snow. Turning it off skips a per-column biome and heightmap sweep around you plus hundreds of transparent quads every frame during a storm. Rain sounds and ground splashes are unaffected.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityDistance.to: How far chests, signs, banners and machines are drawn. Each one costs a pose, a lookup and a pass through its renderer every frame, so cutting this is the strongest lever in a dense base. Minecraft stops at 64 blocks on its own and Block Entity Culling adds a 96-block gate, so this only bites below those.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveVsync.tooltip: With plain V-Sync, one late frame costs a whole refresh interval, so 60 fps drops straight to 30. Adaptive V-Sync presents the late frame immediately instead, trading a brief tear for the frames. Only applies while V-Sync is on, and only on drivers that offer it.
vulkanmod.options.coreShaderPacks.toolti: Lets a resource pack replace the terrain and cloud shaders with its own Sodium-style core shaders. Turn it off to ignore those files and keep Volcanic's own shaders when a pack breaks the display.
vulkanmod.options.anisotropicFiltering.t: Sharpens floors and walls seen at a grazing angle, which mipmaps otherwise blur into mush. On Minecraft's stitched block atlas it can bleed neighbouring sprites into each other at distance, which is why it lives here and not under Quality.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.vsync_off: Needs V-Sync on. Turn V-Sync on under Display to use this.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.present_mode: Your graphics driver does not offer adaptive V-Sync. MoltenVK on macOS never does.
vulkanmod.ui.disabled.anisotropy: This GPU does not support anisotropic filtering.
vulkanmod.options.debugMenu.tooltip: Volcanic's own debug panel: frame timings, hardware and build info. Separate from the vanilla F3 screen.
vulkanmod.options.debugMenuKey.tooltip: Which key opens and closes the debug panel. Set it to Not Bound to leave the panel to this menu alone.
vulkanmod.options.uiAnimations.tooltip: Sliding pages, travelling selection, easing scroll and the rest of the menu's motion. Turn it off and every state change lands instantly.
vulkanmod.options.backgroundAnimation.to: The embers breathing behind the settings, with their sparks, lava pops and smoke. Turn it off to keep the artwork without anything moving on it.
vulkanmod.options.uiSounds.tooltip: The click on every menu control and the theme that plays once the game reaches the title screen. Minecraft's own sounds are untouched.
vulkanmod.options.loadingScreen.tooltip: Volcanic's own startup screen, with its fire and its bar. Turn it off to get Minecraft's back. Another mod that claims the loading screen switches this off on its own.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.intro: Which mods Volcanic recognised in this profile, and every adjustment it made to draw alongside them. Recognising a mod is not a promise that it works.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.empty.hint: Volcanic found no mod that needs special handling, and it made no adjustment to anyone else's rendering.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.tweak.emi: Batched item rendering is off so EMI's stacks draw correctly.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.tweak.flywheel: The instancing backend is off; contraptions draw through the vanilla path.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.tweak.veil: Post-processing and deferred lights are bypassed on the Vulkan backend.
vulkanmod.ui.compat.tweak.polytone: Its texture variants and block offsets are wired into chunk meshing.
